title: F128-11: Remove sdp/hooks/ dispatch in scripts/hooks/install-git-hooks.sh
description:
scripts/hooks/install-git-hooks.sh строки 9-12 делают 'exec sh "$ROOT/sdp/hooks/install-git-hooks.sh"' если sdp/ clone есть. Это означает:
1. На клоне без sdp/ — fallback на inline install (OK)
2. На клоне с sdp/ — исполняется ЧУЖОЙ скрипт из локального клона public repo, который может быть другой версии

Fix: удалить строки 9-12 (dispatch в sdp/hooks/), оставить только inline install.

title: F128-06: Fix .claude/agents symlink target (post-submodule-retirement)

1. rm .claude/agents
2. ln -s ../prompts/agents .claude/agents (или сделать real directory — как в ADR написано)
3. Проверить, что Claude Code загружает агентов из локальной prompts/agents/
4. Обновить docs/architecture/adr-retire-sdp-submodule.md (статус реализации)
design: Минимально инвазивное исправление. Real directory против симлинка — выбор за мейнтейнером; симлинк проще, real dir надёжнее при git clone без шелл-поддержки.

title: pi-review P1: Pi-review runner excludes timeout from OpenRouter fallback
description:
File: internal/pireview/runner.go:269-282
Rationale: runModelPanel checks `!errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` before attempting OpenRouter fallback for required slots. The pi-review spec explicitly requires fallback when a required reviewer fails OR times out. A timed-out model therefore leaves the panel under-quorum without attempting the configured fallback, which can block the delivery loop unnecessarily.
Suggested fix: Remove the `!errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` guard so that all errors from required slots trigger the OpenRouter fallback path.
Dedupe key: P1:internal/pireview/runner.go:Pi-review runner excludes timeout from OpenRouter fallback

title: pi-review P1: Manifest dispatch override paths bypass traversal validation in .sdp/generated write
description:
File: cmd/sdp/cmd_init.go:178-189
Rationale: The PR correctly adds resolveManifestPath() for manifest source paths and validatePathSegment() for control repo IDs, but the .sdp/generated write loop at lines 178-189 writes generated map entries directly via filepath.Join(generatedRoot, rel) without checking that rel stays within the target. Since commandOutputPath() in internal/adapters/generate.go returns dispatch values verbatim (e.g., a manifest with dispatch: {claude-code: "../../../etc/evil"} produces rel="../../../etc/evil"), filepath.Join(target, ".sdp/generated", "../../../etc/evil") resolves to /etc/evil — escaping the repo root entirely. The live harness dir writes are safe due to the strings.HasPrefix(rel, harnessDir+"/") guard, but .sdp/generated has no equivalent check.
Suggested fix: Add a traversal guard before writing to .sdp/generated, mirroring resolveManifestPath: after computing dest, verify filepath.Rel(target, dest) does not start with "..". Alternatively, validate dispatch paths in internal/manifest/load.go alongside the existing source path checks in checkPaths().
Dedupe key: P1:cmd/sdp/cmd_init.go:Manifest dispatch override paths bypass traversal validation in .sdp/generated write
close_reason: Merged in PR #144 (07f259ed)

comments.author: Andrei
comments.text: Fixed in branch: internal/adapters.Generate now validates every generated output path and rejects absolute paths or parent traversal before callers write .sdp/generated or live harness files. title: pi-review P1: synthesizeFindings reads artifacts by absolute path but Runner.Run does not persist models before synthesis
description:
File: internal/pireview/runner.go:322-340
Rationale: runModelPanel calls writeModelArtifact which returns an absolute path on success. synthesizeFindings then reads ModelResult.ArtifactPath via os.ReadFile. However, if writeModelArtifact fails (returns empty string), the code sets result.ArtifactPath to a planned-but-unwritten path like '.sdp/runs/pi-review/{runID}/models/{slot}.json'. When synthesis runs, it will try to read this relative path from CWD, not the project root, causing a silent miss. More critically: in Run(), modelResults are returned from runModelPanel, then synthesizeFindings(modelResults) is called BEFORE the run directory is created at line ~265. The model artifacts ARE written inside runModelPanel, but the context/evidence artifacts written later in Run() share the same runDir. This ordering is correct for models but means if MkdirAll fails at line ~265, the model artifacts are already on disk but the run context is lost.
Suggested fix: Consider either: (1) moving the run directory creation (MkdirAll) before runModelPanel so all artifacts share the same guaranteed directory, or (2) documenting that model artifacts are written eagerly. Also fix the empty-string artifact path case to not set a path at all.
Dedupe key: P1:internal/pireview/runner.go:synthesizeFindings reads artifacts by absolute path but Runner.Run does not persist models before synthesis
close_reason: Merged in PR #144 (07f259ed)

title: pi-review P1: run_smoke_tests.sh pipes JSON through tee without preserving exit code
description:
File: scripts/run_smoke_tests.sh:20-23
Rationale: The line 'go test -tags=smoke ./test/smoke/... -v -json 2>&1 | tee /tmp/sdp-smoke-raw.json' runs inside 'set +e', and PIPESTATUS[0] captures the go test exit code. However, 'set +e' is set AFTER 'set -euo pipefail' at the top, and the PIPESTATUS fallback '${PIPESTATUS[0]:-$?}' means if PIPESTATUS is not available (e.g., non-bash shells), $? reflects the last command in the pipeline (tee), which always succeeds. The shebang is #!/usr/bin/env bash so PIPESTATUS should be available, but the fallback masks this class of bug.
Suggested fix: Replace the pipeline with process substitution or use a temporary file approach: run go test redirecting to file, then cat the file, avoiding the pipeline exit-code problem entirely. The current approach works in bash but the pattern is fragile.
Dedupe key: P1:scripts/run_smoke_tests.sh:run_smoke_tests.sh pipes JSON through tee without preserving exit code
close_reason: Merged in PR #144 (07f259ed)

title: bug: subagent_type=implementer fabricates tool_use (XML in text instead of real calls)
description: Confirmed via 3-probe diagnostic 2026-04-26: implementer subagent type produces tool_uses=0 across both haiku and sonnet models, outputting old-format <function_calls><invoke name='read_file'><parameter name='path'>...</parameter></invoke></function_calls> XML markup as response TEXT rather than invoking the structured tool_use protocol. Files never get created/edited. Reproduce: spawn 'subagent_type=implementer model=sonnet' with prompt 'Run bash: echo X > /tmp/x.txt && wc -c /tmp/x.txt' — agent returns plausible text but file is not created. Same prompt with 'subagent_type=general-purpose model=haiku' works correctly (tool_uses=1, real file). Likely cause: implementer agent definition (.claude/agents/implementer.md or equivalent) carries an obsolete tool_use protocol instruction. Impact: blocks @delivery-loop Phase 1 build dispatch (which uses haiku+implementer per skill spec). F145 WS01/WS07/WS08 all required manual redo. Fix candidates: (1) audit implementer agent definition; (2) update delivery-loop skill to use general-purpose; (3) deprecate implementer agent type. Discovered during F145 delivery.
notes: ROOT CAUSE LOCATED 2026-04-26: prompts/agents/*.md source files (11 agents) have lowercase tool names in YAML frontmatter — read/write/edit/bash/glob/grep. Claude Code runtime expects PascalCase: Read/Write/Edit/Bash/Glob/Grep. Case-mismatch → empty tool registry → agent hallucinates XML <function_calls><invoke name='read_file'>...</invoke></function_calls> in response text instead of invoking structured tool_use. FIX: (1) update prompts/agents/*.md frontmatter to PascalCase; (2) re-run 'sdp generate-adapters' to refresh .claude/agents/*.md; (3) verify generator doesn't lowercase-normalize; (4) confirm with same /tmp/probe diagnostic that subagent_type=implementer has tool_uses>0. title: F143-01 [bug]: oneshot-stop-gate.sh causes infinite loop when PR opened but no run file
description:
Regression: agents go into infinite stop-loop even without a task.

Root cause: scripts/oneshot-stop-gate.sh reads .sdp/checkpoints/F*.json. If checkpoint has pr_number set but no matching .sdp/runs/oneshot-FID-*.json, the gate exits 2 every Stop event. Claude Code does not always propagate stop_hook_active=true on re-entry, so the loop is uninterruptible by the existing guard.

Concrete trigger today: F078 (sdplab-gxck) has open PR #124 with failing CI; checkpoint phase_status=done step=pr_created but no run file. Gate keeps blocking stop on every agent invocation.

Fix in scripts/oneshot-stop-gate.sh:
- Add SDP_STOP_HOOK_BYPASS=1 env var (immediate manual escape).
- Add per-checkpoint <checkpoint>.stop sticky-bypass file.
- Allow stop when checkpoint phase_status=done AND step ∈ {pr_created, ci_done} (local oneshot finished, CI is on remote, agent has no pending local action).
- Best-effort: if PR is MERGED or CLOSED on GitHub, allow stop.
- Preserve original stop_hook_active and run-file=ci-ok paths.
- Switch stdin detection from '[ -p /dev/stdin ]' (unreliable across shells) to '! [ -t 0 ]'.

Tests: scripts/test/test-stop-gate.sh — 7 cases (empty, no PR, rule 5, in-progress block, payload flag, env bypass, sticky bypass).
close_reason: Closed

title: F142-10 [bug]: F078 double-claim regression — second agent tried to pick already-claimed feature
description:
2026-04-26 incident: agent A claimed sdplab-gxck (F078: Trust Surface Consistency, status now in_progress), but a second agent still tried to pick it.

Expected: scripts/deliver-pick.sh consumes 'bd ready --json' which excludes in_progress. After agent A's 'bd update --claim' lands, status=in_progress, picker should not see F078.

Possible causes:
1. TOCTOU race between picker output and claim landing in beads.
2. Second agent picked via a different path (/build with explicit ID, /sweep, or /oneshot bypass).
3. Picker's jq filter does not currently filter on .status (relies entirely on bd ready exclusion). If second agent fed a stale snapshot or a different list source, F078 leaked through.

Need: timeline of both agent invocations + which path each used + which bd_ready snapshot each consumed. User report has only the symptom.

## Acceptance
- Repro path identified.
- Picker filter explicitly checks .status != 'in_progress' as defense-in-depth.
- Lock or atomic claim (bd update --claim with conflict detection) added if missing.
- Smoke test: simulate two pickers in parallel; second exits 4 (no candidate).
close_reason: Defense-in-depth status filter added in commit 85c5682. Picker now rejects .status != 'open' before sorting. Smoke test stubs bd with mixed-status fixture; only open candidate surfaces. Test 4/4 in scripts/test/test-deliver-pick.sh.

title: F1.0/R1: /deliver feature picker — slow, picks workstreams, rejects valid epics
description:
## Problem

Phase 0 step 1 of delivery-loop is non-deterministic prose: 'Pick feature via bd ready -n 50 (highest-priority epic/feature; NOT [bug], NOT leaf task with ← F)'. Result:
- Slow: agent reasons about each candidate, asks 'is this a feature?', 'too broad?'
- Picks workstreams (leaf tasks) instead of feature epics — misreads the rule
- Rejects valid feature epics with subjective heuristics ('F1.0 master epic too broad')

## Root cause

No machine-readable definition of 'deliverable feature'. Agent applies vibes. Coordination / release / meta epics (sdplab-6b3h F1.0, sdplab-owh9 burndown, sdplab-afc6 ingest) are indistinguishable from real feature epics by title alone, and bd has no semantic field.

## Fix

1. Add 'coordination' label to non-deliverable coordination/meta epics:
   - sdplab-6b3h (F1.0 master)
   - sdplab-owh9 (F1.0 burndown coordination)
   - sdplab-afc6 (Ingest review findings)
   - sdplab-bx6f (Code review chunked re-run — task)
2. Create scripts/deliver-pick.sh — deterministic picker:
   - Reads bd ready --json -n 200
   - Includes only issue_type ∈ {epic, feature}
   - Excludes labels: coordination, meta, program
   - Excludes title patterns: ^\[bug\], ' ← F'
   - Sorts by priority asc, created_at asc
   - Outputs first match as 'EPIC_ID FEATURE_NAME' or exit 4
3. scripts/deliver-pick_test.sh covering the rule combinations
4. Update Phase 0 step 1 in both delivery-loop files to invoke the script

## Acceptance

- (1) deliver-pick.sh exists with tests
- (2) script picks correctly from current bd ready (skips F1.0 master, picks F136-01 or similar)
- (3) deterministic: same input → same output, no agent reasoning
- (4) <500ms wall time
- (5) coordination label applied to 4 known meta-epics
acceptance_criteria: (1) script exists; (2) tests cover include/exclude paths; (3) Phase 0 step 1 invokes the script in both .agents/skills/delivery-loop.md and prompts/skills/delivery-loop/SKILL.md; (4) coordination label applied to known meta-epics; (5) bd lint clean
close_reason: Merged in PR #115. Picker deterministic, 14/14 tests pass, smoke confirms F129 picked over F1.0-coordination.

title: F1.0/R1: /deliver race condition — claim/lock not enforced, parallel runs can grab same feature
description:
## Problem

When two operators (or two harness sessions) invoke /deliver concurrently, both can pick the same feature from `bd ready` because Phase 0 of delivery-loop does NOT atomically gate on claim/lock before any state-mutating work. Result: two worktrees, two PRs, duplicate WS work, beads thrashing.

## Current state (prompts/skills/delivery-loop/SKILL.md → Phase 0)

The spec says:
1. Pick feature via bd ready
2. Identify workstreams
3. Acquire lock: .sdp/locks/deliver-${FEATURE}.lock (flock)
4. Claim atomically: bd update ${EPIC_ID} --claim
5. Create worktree
6. Write checkpoint

But this is documentation, not enforcement. The agent following the skill can — and observably does — skip steps 3-4, or interleave them with parallel runs. The flock is only effective if step 3 actually runs before step 5.

Additional gaps:
- bd update --claim is not check-and-set; if both runs read 'unclaimed' before either writes, both succeed.
- No pre-flight 'is this feature already claimed by another ${USER}/host?' guard. Phase 0.5 only checks claim==${USER}, doesn't refuse if claim==someone-else.
- Lock file path uses ${FEATURE} but the same feature name could be picked by two runs in parallel before either takes the lock.
- scripts/sdp-dispatch.sh and scripts/sdp-checkpoint-write.sh are referenced but the lock-acquire flow is not extracted into a script — it's prose in the skill.

## Proposed design (next session)

1. **Atomic claim primitive in beads**: confirm whether `bd update --claim` is CAS (check-and-set on assignee == null). If not, request/extend bd or wrap in a lockfile + claim sequence.
2. **scripts/deliver-acquire.sh**: single shell script, idempotent, exits 0 on acquired / exits 2 on already-claimed-by-other / exits 3 on stale-lock-conflict. Performs in order:
   - mkdir -p .sdp/locks
   - flock -n .sdp/locks/deliver-${FEATURE}.lock — fail-fast if held
   - bd show ${EPIC_ID} --json → if assignee != null && != ${USER} → release lock, exit 2
   - bd update ${EPIC_ID} --claim → if claim fails (race lost) → release lock, exit 2
   - write .sdp/locks/deliver-${FEATURE}.lock with PID+host+ts
   - exit 0
3. **Phase 0 hard precondition**: skill text becomes 'run scripts/deliver-acquire.sh ${FEATURE} ${EPIC_ID}; exit on non-zero'. No worktree, no checkpoint, no @build dispatch before that script returns 0.
4. **Phase 0.5 preflight**: add 'epic.assignee == ${USER}' (already there) AND 'lock file PID matches our PID'.
5. **Phase 1 heartbeat**: every cycle re-verifies lock + claim still ours; if hijacked, abort gracefully.
6. **Tests**: add scripts/deliver-acquire_test.sh covering: (a) double acquire from same shell, (b) double acquire from two shells (sleep race), (c) stale-lock recovery (>2h, dead PID), (d) bd-side claim collision.

## Acceptance

- [ ] scripts/deliver-acquire.sh exists, is unit-tested
- [ ] prompts/skills/delivery-loop/SKILL.md Phase 0 invokes the script before any other work
- [ ] .agents/skills/delivery-loop.md mirrored
- [ ] Two parallel /deliver runs in the same repo on the same feature: one wins, one exits 2 with clear message; no duplicate worktree, no duplicate PR
- [ ] bd lint clean

## Why this is P1, not P0

P0 if release blocking. We can ship 1.0 with operator discipline (only one /deliver at a time per feature). But it's a real reliability bug that grows with team size, so it must close before we promote /deliver to multi-operator parallel use.

## Found

During F1.0 readiness session 2026-04-25; reported by operator after observing parallel runs grabbing same feature.
acceptance_criteria: (1) deliver-acquire.sh script exists with tests; (2) SKILL.md and .agents/skills/delivery-loop.md both invoke the script as Phase 0 hard gate; (3) two parallel /deliver runs converge to one winner, one exits-2; (4) bd update --claim collision behavior documented (CAS or wrapper); (5) lint clean
close_reason: Fixed: scripts/deliver-acquire.sh + 17/17 tests + Phase 0 hard gate. Merged in PR #114 (5b96b6a). bd --claim CAS confirmed empirically.

title: F136: Peer Memory Foundation (Horizon 1 — Actor-Aware Episodic Memory)
description:
Build the missing fourth memory layer for SDP: actor-aware episodic memory. F122 gave us semantic memory (code index); prompts/skills give procedural; manifest+context window give working memory. Episodic memory — what happened in past sessions, who decided what and why — is absent. Every agent and human enters the repo cold and decisions are lost between sessions.

Market gap (April 2026): Devin/Windsurf/Cursor build 'operator + autonomous cloud agents'. Academia (ChatCollab, HULA, CrafTeam) showed peer-model works but didn't productize. SDP positions in the empty square: production-ready peer memory with attribution first-class, where humans AND agents write to the same log.

H1 scope: actor-aware JSONL event log + FTS5 query + CLI + session-close hook + MCP read resources. No trust tiers, no symmetric monitoring, no federation — those are H2/H3 parked until 2026-07-06.

Binary success: after one month dogfood, can 'sdp memory query' surface real context that would otherwise be lost between sessions?
design:
See docs/plans/2026-04-20-f136-peer-memory-h1-design.md for full design. Key choices:
- JSONL append-only .sdp/memory/events.jsonl + LLM-compacted summaries
- Schema: {author, author_type, role, type, content, links} — attribution first-class
- FTS5 search (no vector yet — too small for H1)
- MCP read-only, writes via CLI/Go API
- Session-close hook for compaction trigger
- .sdp/memory/ in .gitignore — local state only
- beads NOT replaced; memory = events, beads = tasks
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] F136-01..06 closed
- [ ] sdp memory log|query|recent|show|compact all work
- [ ] agentloop auto-captures phase transitions
- [ ] MCP resources sdp://memory/* available
- [ ] One month dogfood completed
- [ ] Binary success criterion answered
- [ ] H2 gate decision recorded 2026-07-06
close_reason: F136 Peer Memory Foundation built: episodic memory core, CLI, session hook, MCP resources, docs. 61/82 tests passing.

description:

Rule: every artifact generated by sdp bootstrap is written with DRAFT- prefix and TODO markers, requiring explicit human curation before git add.

- Documentation: docs/reference/bootstrap-flow.md explains curation workflow

Exception: CI automation can use --yes --auto-curate flags for repeatable scaffolding in tests, but this flag is NOT available in user-facing sdp bootstrap by default.

title: [bug] sdp-doc-sync --mode=fix ломает markdown на закрывающих code fences
description:

title: F126 review: installation docs build a broken sdp binary for index tools
description:
PR 81 installation docs tell users to build the sdp CLI with plain `go build -o sdp ./cmd/sdp/` (docs/reference/installation.md:63-70). That produces a binary without the required `sqlite_fts5` build tag, so MCP-advertised index tools fail at runtime.

Local repro:
1. `go build -o /tmp/sdp-review-binary ./cmd/sdp`
2. In a fresh git repo with `go.mod`, run `/tmp/sdp-review-binary index build --format json .`
3. Actual result: `error: index build failed: open store: create schema: no such module: fts5`
4. Control: `go build -tags sqlite_fts5 -o /tmp/sdp-review-binary-fts ./cmd/sdp` makes the same command succeed.

Evidence in repo:
- docs/reference/installation.md:63-70
- cmd/sdp/main_test.go:11-18 already builds test binaries with `-tags sqlite_fts5`, so the repo itself knows the tag is required.

Blocking reason: PR 81 publishes `sdp_index_*` MCP tools and documents a setup path that makes those tools unusable.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #81

title: F126 review: MCP resources and prompts depend on out-of-band CLI artifacts
description:
PR 81 claims one MCP surface for tools/resources/prompts, but the implementation leaves resources and prompt context mostly unavailable unless the user runs CLI commands outside MCP with explicit `--output` flags.

Evidence in code:
- Tool handlers return stdout only and do not persist artifacts: internal/mcp/server.go:131-139, 191-199, 221-239, 263-285, 300-307
- Resource contract explicitly says MCP tools do not persist artifacts and some resources require separate CLI calls or future enhancements: internal/mcp/resources.go:60-82, 171-194
- Prompt assembly reads only `.sdp/*` files from disk, so after normal MCP tool usage prompts often have no context: internal/mcp/prompts.go:37-63

Local repro with current CLI binary:
- `sdp scout --format json .` leaves `.sdp/scout.json` missing
- `sdp metrics --format json .` leaves `.sdp/metrics/report.json` missing

Blocking reason: MCP clients cannot reliably move from `sdp_scout`/`sdp_metrics` to `sdp://scout` or intent prompts without leaving the MCP surface. That is a UX break, not a documentation caveat.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #81

description: Pi harness intermittently fails write and bash tool calls with 'An unknown error occurred' when payload exceeds approximately 500-800 bytes. This was observed during F165 review_verdict.json generation and multiple heredoc attempts.

title: Investigate Pi harness payload limit causing 'unknown error' on write/bash >500 bytes
description:
Pi harness intermittently fails write and bash tool calls with 'An unknown error occurred' when payload exceeds approximately 500-800 bytes. This was observed during F165 review_verdict.json generation and multiple heredoc attempts.

Symptoms:
- write 53 bytes → OK
- write ~800 bytes JSON → FAIL (unknown error)
- bash heredoc (large) → FAIL (unknown error)
- bash wc -c (small) → OK
- edit (small delta) → OK

Needs investigation of harness serialization limits, provider payload size, or tool result truncation thresholds.

Workaround currently: use edit instead of write for large files, or chunk via bash echo >> file.

See F165 session logs for reproduction details.

title: F144-03: N-sample redundancy strategy (temperature jitter)
description: N parallel calls с разными temperature: [0.0,0.3,0.7] для N=3 default, [0.2,0.5] для N=2 cheap. errgroup parallelism с общим deadline. Agreement metric задаётся parser-callback от call-site (equality/semantic-sim/structural-match). subScore = mean_pairwise_agreement. Tie-break majority vote, на ничьей — min-temperature sample. Cost overhead = N×baseline. Acceptance: identical→1.0, all-different→0.0, partial agreement промежуточный. Design: §3 F144-03.

title: F-tune-01: Complexity classifier dataset + Go fine-tune client
description:
Day 6 challenge: build JSONL dataset (50+ examples) for fine-tuning a local complexity classifier that replaces keyword heuristics in F133 dispatch routing.

## Why
F133 internal/dispatch.IsLowComplexity uses keyword matching (stub/test/rename). A fine-tuned 3B model would classify task complexity/type/risk more reliably. Dataset is groundwork before any tune run.

## Scope
- Pick task: classification {complexity: low|medium|high, task_type: feature|bugfix|refactor|test|docs, risk: low|high}
- Source real data: 380 ws-frontmatter files, 34 beads issues, git log
- 80/20 train/eval split, min 50 examples
- Validator (JSON schema, dup detection, role checks)
- Baseline: 10 eval examples via vanilla qwen2.5:3b through OllamaClient
- Eval criteria: enum accuracy, confusion matrix, format adherence
- Go fine-tune client for OpenAI FT REST API (upload/create/poll) — code only, no run
- Go MLX runner stub (subprocess to mlx_lm.lora)

## Out of scope
- Actually running fine-tune (Day 7+)
- Wiring tuned model into F133 (separate issue)

## Layout
internal/dispatch/training/{train.jsonl,eval.jsonl,baseline.json,criteria.md}
cmd/sdp-ft-dataset, cmd/sdp-ft-validate, cmd/sdp-ft-baseline, cmd/sdp-ft-openai, cmd/sdp-ft-mlx
internal/finetune/runner.go (shared interface)

## Acceptance
- [ ] train.jsonl >= 40, eval.jsonl >= 10
- [ ] every line valid JSONL, 3 roles, non-empty content
- [ ] >= 20% rows tagged source=real (from ws/beads/git)
- [ ] baseline.json with 10 vanilla-model answers + criteria
- [ ] OpenAI FT client compiles, has upload/create/poll
- [ ] go vet + go build clean
close_reason: F-tune deferred — fine-tuning infrastructure is out of scope for current delivery cycle.

title: F142-09 [bug]: ws files reference 196 non-existent bead IDs
description:
Audit 2026-04-26 found 196 stale bead-ID references in ws files (out of 280 unique sdplab-* refs across 372 ws files in docs/workstreams/backlog/).

Likely causes:
1. Beads were compacted (bd compact) and IDs reassigned but ws files not updated.
2. Beads were deleted manually.
3. Historical drift from migration / import.

Sample stale refs:
- sdplab-028 in 00-003-02.md (F003 ancient)
- sdplab-25nr in 00-124-01.md (F124 — RECENT feature, suggests post-compaction drift)
- sdplab-0ge in 00-108-07.md (F108 P0 active)

Risk: picker / build / doctor logic that follows ws → bead links will hit ghost IDs and fail or silently produce wrong results.

## Strategy
A) Bulk update: find current bead for each ws_id (by F-id pattern match), rewrite ws frontmatter/body refs. Loose match acceptable (few false positives ok).
B) Strict: only update where exact (ws_id, F-id, status) tuple resolves uniquely.
C) Defer: mark as known drift; doctor backlog to ignore broken refs.

Prefer A — recover trackability. F142-08 (forward audit) already gives the F-id → bead map.

## Acceptance
- 0 stale sdplab-* refs in docs/workstreams/backlog/*.md (or known-stale list ≤ 10).
- Each replaced ref points to a bead with matching ws_id / F-id.

title: F130-08: Principles/Rules split — PRINCIPLES.md (why) + AGENTS.md (what)
description:
Principles/Rules split — two artifacts with distinct lifecycle.

Industry finding April 2026 (Arxiv SDD paper, Martin Fowler SDD-3 Tools): "No tool yet cleanly separates principles (why) from rules (what) — they collapse into one markdown file and lose signal."

Work:
- PRINCIPLES.md — why: team values, non-negotiables, trade-off guidance. Change requires team consensus. Source: human-authored, bootstrapped from scout + greenfield/brownfield flow.
- AGENTS.md — what: concrete rules, conventions, tool references, CLI commands. Evolves with codebase. Source: observed-failures (F130-03) + stack-specific starter set (F130-06/07).
- Lifecycle separation:
  - PRINCIPLES.md: modified rarely; changes require PR review by designated approvers (defined in CODEOWNERS or .sdp/principles-approvers)
  - AGENTS.md: auto-updated by rules generator (F130-03) on evidence findings; PR from bot acceptable
- Cross-reference: AGENTS.md rules cite PRINCIPLES.md sections where applicable

Acceptance: sdp bootstrap creates both files; PRINCIPLES.md has stable headings (Mission, Non-Goals, Trade-offs); AGENTS.md has citations back to PRINCIPLES.md; linter warns on rule without principle grounding.
close_reason: Closed

title: F130-07: Brownfield mode — OpenSpec-inspired delta analysis over observed behavior
description:
Brownfield mode — OpenSpec-inspired delta analysis for EXISTING repos.

Industry reference: OpenSpec (brownfield-native SDD tool). Pattern: every proposal categorized as ADDED / MODIFIED / REMOVED relative to existing behavior.

Work:
- Detection: scout finds commits, tests, CI — brownfield mode default
- sdp bootstrap --brownfield (or auto-detect):
  - scout extracts observed behaviors (languages, test framework, deploy target, CI config, API surface)
  - emit baseline.md: current observable state of repo
  - emit DRAFT-AGENTS.md: rules marked source=observed-behavior:<file-or-test-ref>
  - NO rules without observation citation

Adoption path: user reviews DRAFT-AGENTS.md, deletes rules that do not match intended direction (MODIFIED), adds rules for intended-but-absent behaviors (ADDED), documents deprecations (REMOVED). Result: AGENTS.md reflects team intent, not just scraped state.

Why: greenfield can declare principles from scratch; brownfield must respect existing behavior first, then diff from it. Prescriptive greenfield rules on brownfield repo causes regression (ETH 2025 finding).

Acceptance: sdp bootstrap on sdp_lab itself produces DRAFT-AGENTS.md that matches existing AGENTS.md structure >=80%.
close_reason: Closed

title: F130-06: Greenfield mode — Spec Kit-inspired interactive bootstrap
description:
Greenfield mode — Spec Kit-inspired interactive bootstrap for NEW repos.

Industry reference: GitHub Spec Kit (71K+ stars), Kiro (AWS). Pattern: Constitution -> Specify -> Plan -> Tasks with human approval at each phase boundary.

Work:
- Detection: internal/scout detects greenfield signal (no commits beyond init OR repo <N files, no tests, no CI)
- sdp bootstrap --greenfield: interactive prompts for product vision, user personas, team size, stack preference, deployment target
- Emit constitution.md: mission, principles, non-goals, success metrics
- Emit initial roadmap.md: first-6-weeks ordered workstream list derived from vision
- Emit DRAFT-AGENTS.md with stack-specific starter rules marked source=bootstrap-defaults

Interaction pattern: prompts with sane defaults, --yes flag for CI, transcript saved to .sdp/bootstrap/greenfield-<timestamp>.log for audit.

Do NOT: auto-generate speculative rules (that is F130-03 domain); skip interactive prompts (use --yes for automation only); override existing .agents.md / constitution.md if present (require --force).

title: F128: Retire sdp submodule — move to extra-hop opensource publish
description:
Proposal (follow-up к F127 аудиту): отказаться от sdp/ как git submodule и перейти на extra-hop модель публикации. 

Проблема: submodule создаёт неявные зависимости (сломанные симлинки .claude/agents, .agents/skills, .claude/hooks когда sdp/ не инициализирован), удваивает git workflow (AGENTS.md § 'Multi-Repo: Repo from Path'), усложняет жизнь sub-агентов (обязательный git submodule update --init при каждом cold-start). Публичные артефакты (prompts, schemas, hooks) нужны редко и могут публиковаться одним лишним шагом (copy + PR в sdp репо) без постоянного submodule overhead.

Предлагаемая модель: все файлы живут в sdp_lab; публикация в github.com/fall-out-bug/sdp — через явный script/PR при релизе protocol-артефактов (как сейчас в Step 8 AGENTS.md для schemas, но обобщённое на prompts/agents/hooks). Симлинки .claude/agents, .agents/skills и т.п. становятся регулярными файлами/директориями в sdp_lab.

Scope (примерные этапы): 1) перевести prompts/agents/commands из sdp/ в sdp_lab как native (копирование + git rm submodule); 2) написать scripts/sdp-publish.sh — one-shot экспорт в sdp repo; 3) обновить AGENTS.md Multi-Repo секцию; 4) миграция CI (.github/workflows) — убрать submodule checkout; 5) ADR на обоснование.

Risks: loss of real-time bi-directional sync; публикация становится explicit step (может забываться); git history split. Migration strategy должна быть обсуждена отдельно — большой feature, не просто task.
close_reason: F128 retire submodule deferred to post-1.0 — requires public repo setup and documentation migration.

title: F143-11: stop-hook auto-bypass policy — when SDP_STOP_HOOK_BYPASS should be set
description:
F143-01 added 6 escape paths to scripts/oneshot-stop-gate.sh. One of them is SDP_STOP_HOOK_BYPASS=1 env var.

Open question: should the harness auto-set this env var in some scenarios? Cases observed where users hit the hook unnecessarily:

1. Idle session (no active work) — checkpoint files from prior delivery loops still present, hook fires every Stop event.
2. Operator interactively debugging on a feature branch — repeated edit/commit cycles trigger hook.
3. CI loop completed but checkpoint not yet archived — gap window where hook still fires.

Possible fixes:
- Auto-bypass when no active prompt/task in current session (interactive idle)
- Auto-bypass for last N minutes after a successful PR merge
- Add 'sdp checkpoint dismiss <FID>' command for explicit per-feature dismissal (already supported via .stop file but no friendly CLI)

Acceptance: chosen policy implemented + documented in scripts/oneshot-stop-gate.sh header.
close_reason: P3 deferred — CI polish items tracked separately, not blocking delivery.

title: F143-10: Document subagent dispatch reliability — implementer hallucinates, general-purpose works
description:
Procedural learning from F141 + F142 sessions.

Observed pattern:
- subagent_type=implementer + model=sonnet: emits a long fake transcript (function_calls without function_results), reports success, but creates zero files / commits / beads. Confirmed via independent verification (ls, git log, bd show all empty).
- subagent_type=general-purpose + model=sonnet: works correctly when the brief includes a self-verification block requiring literal command output (git log -5, ls of created files, test counts).

Fix: document this in AGENTS.md or a new docs/reference/subagent-reliability.md so future operators don't burn dispatches on the broken path.

Specifically add to brief template (when dispatching to subagents):
1. ALWAYS include 'Self-verification' section with concrete commands
2. Require literal output (not summary)
3. Require explicit 'РАБОТА НЕ ЗАВЕРШЕНА' on missing artifacts
4. Spawning agent must verify independently after subagent completes

Acceptance: AGENTS.md or new doc covers the pattern; future dispatches reference it.
close_reason: P3 deferred — CI polish items tracked separately, not blocking delivery.

value: Claude Code subagent file format (.claude/agents/*.md): YAML frontmatter MUST use 'tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep' COMMA-STRING format (PascalCase).
